title: Friction material substitution driven by substance restriction
engineering_question: A material specification has been changed for regulatory reasons. Which requirements are affected and is the existing verification evidence still valid?
one_liner: Review the verification implications of this design change.
initial_input: Engineering change ECR-002 replaces the front brake friction compound with a low-copper formulation to meet market restrictions on restricted substances.
expected_impacted_domains: Supplier process control on the moulding operation
expected_reasoning_paths: The regulatory driver is satisfied - TR-021 passes REQ-064 - but the change creates consequential effects on adjacent requirements
REQ-060 and REQ-061 pass, so the approval-critical requirements are currently met
REQ-063 and REQ-067 fail via TR-017 and TR-022, so the change trades regulatory compliance against perceived quality
TR-018 is inconclusive because the friction band definition does not extend above 400 degC, which is a specification gap rather than a test failure
known_unknowns: TEST-063 objective blending discontinuity limit is TBD_PROGRAMME_SPECIFIC
The friction coefficient specification band does not define behaviour above 400 degC
No wear rate data for the revised compound exists in the environment
data_classification: SIMULATED ENTERPRISE ARTEFACT - not OEM, customer or proprietary data
